parsed.explanation: The combined regime is not just hostile climate: national passport/visa screening can refuse or investigate a trans visitor, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and the division’s public-facility law reaches airports and government buildings, imposing birth-sex facility rules enforced by private bounty suits and civil/criminal penalties. Immigration custody has documented abuse. National hate-crime and anti-discrimination protections and pending litigation exist, but none is shown to stop the facility, bounty, or border exposure in real time. This is High Risk: safer than mandatory-imprisonment anchors, but less safe than denial-entry-only or working-protection anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas; new X markers are not processed; discrepancy can prompt refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, with reports of confiscation and stranded travellers. Division law invalidates state IDs mismatching birth sex.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements with limited waivers; litigation is pending. No documented working border remedy for an outed visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport meets national screening, then division public-building and ID checks; officer discretion at an airport can chain refusal, investigation, or facility exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections policies remove hormones and impose conversion-like treatment on trans inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court challenges exist, but no operative custody protection is documented; national hate-crime law does not reach custody abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can escalate into immigration detention, where birth-sex custody rules and documented abuse compound the outing.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in public buildings including airports, schools and government offices; penalties up to $1,000 and private bounty suits by any person. A similar state arrest shows enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.protection: A lawsuit was filed but no ruling or injunction is recorded; state public-accommodation law does not neutralize the facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airport transit triggers both national border screening and division facility/bounty exposure in the same public building.

care_services.exposure: National orders stigmatize gender-affirming care, restrict minors, threaten funding and insurance, and subpoena records; division bans care for minors though enjoined. Hospital ward placement can out a traveller.
care_services.protection: Some injunctions block the minor care ban and national orders; adult emergency care is not shown as categorically denied.
care_services.interaction: A medical emergency in the division can combine sex-segregated facility rules with a hostile care climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders and counterterrorism language frame 'radically pro-transgender' activity as a security concern; school transition support is directed for prosecution; official hostility raises reporting and outing risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; counterterrorism guidance says mere disagreement is not targeted; courts have enjoined some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing can make police or border contact more perilous for an outed visitor, though there is no general criminal ban on trans status.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors in division public buildings, including airports, face birth-sex facility rules, fines and bounty suits; national care bans and school-prosecution orders increase family outing risk. A guardian travelling with a trans minor shares the exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: The minor care ban is enjoined; no facility or bounty remedy is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent accompanying a trans minor through an airport restroom or ID check can trigger both facility enforcement and national document scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime law excludes gender identity; national coverage exists but state enforcement varies. A documented bathroom arrest and custody humiliation show police can be the enforcing actor.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; division law prohibits gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations since 2020.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police called to a facility dispute may enforce the ban rather than protect the traveller; recourse is partial and not shown working for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The division lawsuit is unresolved; no enforcement data exists for facility/ID provisions; bounty-suit volume is unknown; no injunction blocks the law. Visitor remedies are uncertain and slow.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, legal-aid guidance, national hate-crime law, and state anti-discrimination law exist, but are not documented as operative for facility or border exposures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate after detention or suit and do not prevent airport/facility outing or border refusal.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor mandates severe multi-year imprisonment and possible capital escalation for outed travellers. This dossier lacks a general criminal ban on trans status and has no execution pathway, so it is safer; but facility penalties, bounty suits, border fraud ineligibility and custody abuse keep it well below low-risk.

That anchor has explicit no-detention safeguards for document mismatch but still denies entry and retains papers. This jurisdiction is less safe: national screening can escalate to fraud or removal, and the division facility law adds criminal/civil bounty exposure in airports and public buildings.

That anchor shows a working non-discrimination code overriding a registry mismatch. Here paper protections exist but do not reach the facility ban or border discretion; the operative rule is birth-sex facility restriction with private enforcement.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines national border/document screening with a division law that turns public facilities—including airports—into sites of birth-sex exclusion enforced by private bounty suits and criminal/civil penalties. A trans visitor outed at a checkpoint or restroom can face refusal, investigation, fines, suits, or custody; immigration custody has documented abuse. National hate-crime and anti-discrimination protections and pending litigation exist, but no remedy is shown to stop the facility or border exposure in real time. The rating is High Risk, below denial-entry-only anchors and above mandatory-imprisonment anchors.
